newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on pre-holiday swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on pre-holiday swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply firmer across the board amid light dealing on Monday, as brokers switched from dollars to pesos for swap trading ahead of the forthcoming long weekend, traders said.
"Dollars were in supply from early on because a long weekend is coming up and that will make swaps attractive tomorrow," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 3.5 and 3.2 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8900/7.8920 and 7.8860/7.8900 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 3.5 centavos firmer at 7.8885/7.8920 per dollar.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on March 27 and 28 for Holy Thursday and Good Friday.
Dealers said the market was calm ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday, as a hike in base rates had already been discounted.
Nonetheless, they added trade was slow on caution over the outcome of domestic primary rates at Tuesday evening's central bank auction.

"Technically, a (FOMC) hike has been discounted. Nonetheless, we do see pressure for the peso, as we are approaching the close of the month and the quarter, and have yet to see what happens at the primary auction," another trader said.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders in Mexico City showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 289-day Cetes rates at an average of 21.04 percent. This would be a fall of 66 basis points since last week's auction.
Auction results are due at 1830 local time/0030 GMT. Traders said they expected 48-hour peso contracts to weaken against the dollar on Tuesday due to pre-weekend swaps.
